evidence_items.locator: Section IV-B2, RQ2; qualification in Section V, Threats to validity
evidence_items.explanation: ObfusEval compares functionality-preserving alterations of code from real projects and finds lower test-pass rates. This supports a familiarity disadvantage, although the authors acknowledge that obfuscation can also change complexity.

CTF-Code finds deterioration after small requirement changes to easy programming problems. This supports sensitivity to unfamiliar variants, but it does not directly establish training exposure or measure complete application development.

evidence_items.explanation: RealClassEval reports little practical difference between codebases classified as seen and unseen, challenging a broad familiarity explanation. The exact experiment date is unavailable, so this is contextual counterevidence rather than a dated contradiction within the target period.

unresolved_gaps: The supporting studies do not fully isolate familiarity from complexity or requirement sensitivity.
